title: Hot Cocoa Mix

drivers.name: Competitor store opening across the street
drivers.evidence: New competitor entry in the same location; no prior data on impact, but store competition is a known demand reducer. Noise-adjusted effect shrunk due to limited evidence (one occurrence).

adjustment.analysis: The baseline median is 30.5. No events are scheduled. The price is up 3.4% (to $5.20), which historically has not driven uplift—past price hikes showed no lift. A competitor opened across the street, a clear demand risk. Past 'ordinary' weeks with similar price points (e.g., 2026-09-28, 2026-10-05) saw no sales spike. The past promotion effects are noise-adjusted to x1.0. The Thanksgiving week before had no lasting uplift (noise-adjusted x1.0). However, a new competitor entry is a known demand reducer. Evidence is thin (one event, no prior data on similar openings), so shrink effect toward 1.0. Downside spread widens slightly due to uncertainty.

brief:
PRODUCT: Hot Cocoa Mix | category Grocery | Store #12 (Austin, TX)
TARGET WEEK: 2026-11-16 to 2026-11-22 (6 weeks after the last week with sales data)

KNOWN PLAN FOR THE TARGET WEEK:
  events: none
  shelf price: 5.20 (+3.4% vs regular price 5.03)
  planner notes: A competitor opens a store across the street this week

STATISTICAL BASELINE (exponential smoothing of recent sales; it ignores events, promotions and prices):
  median 30.5 | 5%-95%: 1.3 - 49.2 | 10%-90%: 6.3 - 48.7

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-77% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
